Kuvitus: laboratorion pöydällä seisoo te: Illustration: on a laboratory bench a vertical copper tube stands in a stand, with a transparent plastic tube beside it. A small magnet is just emerging from the lower end of the copper tube above a soft pad. On the bench is a stopwatch showing that several seconds have passed.
Kaksi periaatekuvaa, ei mittakaavassa. K: Two schematic diagrams, not to scale. The copper ring is cut in the plane of the paper, so the cross-sections of its upper and lower edges are visible. On the left a magnet moves towards the ring, north pole first. The induced current in the ring flows into the paper in the upper edge and out of the paper in the lower edge, and its magnetic field at the centre of the ring points to the left, towards the magnet: the side of the ring facing the magnet is a north pole, and the ring repels the magnet. The force on the magnet points to the left, against the motion. On the right the magnet moves away from the ring. The current is in the opposite direction, the field of the ring points to the right, the side facing the magnet is a south pole, and the ring attracts the magnet back. The force points to the right, again against the motion.
Periaatekuva, ei mittakaavassa. Vasemmal: Schematic diagram, not to scale. On the left, a vertical copper tube cut lengthwise, with a magnet falling inside it, north pole downwards. Below the magnet an eddy current circulates in the wall of the tube; it flows into the paper in the right wall and out of the paper in the left wall, and its field points upwards, towards the magnet. Above the magnet the eddy current circulates in the opposite direction, and its field points downwards. The weight acts on the magnet downwards and an equally large braking force upwards, and its velocity points downwards. On the right, the lower eddy-current ring seen from above: the current circulates anticlockwise, and at the centre of the ring the field points towards the viewer, that is, upwards.
Pylväskuvaaja mittakaavassa: energiat, k: Bar chart to scale: the energies when a 20 g magnet has fallen through a tube one metre long. In the plastic tube the decrease of 196 mJ in potential energy has been converted entirely into kinetic energy, and no internal energy is produced. In the copper tube the potential energy decreases by the same amount, but the kinetic energy is only 0.2 mJ, so little that the bar cannot be seen, and almost all of it, 196 mJ, has been converted into internal energy of the tube.
Kaksi periaatekuvaa muuntajan rautasydäm: Two schematic diagrams of the cross-section of the iron core of a transformer, not to scale. The alternating magnetic field points along the core into the paper, shown by the green crosses. On the left a solid iron core: one large eddy-current loop circulates around the whole cross-section. On the right the core is built from thin laminations with an insulating layer between them: the eddy currents circulate only inside each narrow lamination, as small and weak loops.
Kuvitus: induktioliesi, jonka lasipinnal: Illustration: an induction hob with a steel pan on its glass surface. Water is boiling in the pan and steam is rising from it. Under the glass surface a copper coil is shown in cross-section. There is no flame or glowing plate.
